newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi, U.S. rights group in pact.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi, U.S. rights group in pact.

text.p: Civil rights leader the Rev. Jesse Jackson said Wednesday that his Rainbow/PUSH Coalition would end its boycott of Mitsubishi Motors Corp as part of an agreement with Mitsubishi's U.S. unit over alleged sexual harassment and racial discrimination at its U.S. plants.
Jackson said the accord would be a catalyst for more than $200 million in new investments, salaries and jobs for minorities.
As part of the agreement, Mitsubishi has agreed to set a five-year target to increase the proportion of minority- and female-owned Mitsubishi dealerships in the U.S. to 15 percent.
Mitsubishi has also agreed to increase recruitment and training of minorities in the U.S. and to funnel more of its contracts to minority businesses.
Mitsubishi said it would start talks immediately to bring back several women employees who have left their jobs or are on leave and involved in harassment litigation against Mitsubishi.
The agreement was announced at a joint press conference attended by Jackson and Mitsubishi officials.
